summary: This Wikipedia article describes montane ecosystems, which occur on mountain slopes, where temperature decreases with elevation and creates stratified life zones. It covers montane forests (temperate, Mediterranean, and subtropical/tropical, including cloud forests), the subalpine zone below the tree line, and alpine grasslands and tundra above it. It also notes climate change threats and examples of montane ecosystems worldwide.
one_line: Overview of mountain ecosystems, their elevation-driven life zones, montane forests, subalpine zones, and alpine tundra.
key_facts: Montane ecosystems are found on the slopes of mountains, and temperatures fall as elevation increases, causing the ecosystem to stratify.
In middle latitudes, moving up 100 meters on a mountain is roughly equivalent to moving 80 kilometers (0.75° of latitude) toward the nearest pole.
Holdridge defines the climate of montane forest as having a biotemperature of between 6 and 12 °C (43 and 54 °F).
The biotemperature of the subalpine zone is between 3 and 6 °C (37 and 43 °F).
The biotemperature of the alpine zone is between 1.5 and 3 °C (34.7 and 37.4 °F).
Climates with biotemperatures below 1.5 °C (35 °F) tend to consist purely of rock and ice.
The elevation where trees fail to grow is called the tree line.

A region in the Hengduan Mountains adjoining Asia's Tibetan Plateau has been identified as the world's oldest continuous alpine ecosystem, with a community of 3000 plant species, some co-existing for 30 million years.
In the tropics, the lower limit of montane rainforests on large mountains is generally between 1,500 and 2,500 metres, while the upper limit is usually from 2,400 to 3,300 metres.
Montane forests outside Europe tend to be more species-rich, because Europe during the Pleistocene offered smaller-area refugia from the glaciers.
Reduction in cloudiness may already be affecting the Monteverde cloud forest in Costa Rica.
In the Sierra Nevada of California, montane forest has dense stands of lodgepole pine and red fir, while the subalpine zone contains sparse stands of whitebark pine.
Tuolumne Meadows in the Sierra Nevada of California is an example of a subalpine meadow.
Cushion plants look like ground-hugging clumps of moss and escape strong winds blowing a few inches above them.
Lichens' enclosed algal cells can photosynthesize at temperatures as low as −10 °C (14 °F).
Repeated footsteps often destroy tundra plants, and recovery may take hundreds of years.
The most extensive montane grasslands and shrublands occur in the Neotropical páramo of the Andes Mountains.
